description: Neapolitan flatbread baked with tomato, fior di latte mozzarella, basil and olive oil — created as a tribute to Queen Margherita of Savoy.

ingredients.amount: a generous handful, added after the bake
ingredients.name: fresh basil leaves

name: Pizza Margherita
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the water. into a bowl combine flour and salt, pour in the yeasted water, and mix until shaggy; knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and supple.
Knead 8–10 minutes until smooth, then bulk-ferment 1 hour at room temperature. Divide into 2 equal balls and refrigerate, covered, 12–24 hours.
At least 45 minutes before baking, place a pizza steel or stone on a tray in the oven and preheat to maximum (at least 275 °C).
Crush the tomatoes lightly in a bowl with a good pinch of salt and half the oil — the sauce stays raw, like in Napoli.
Stretch one dough ball to a 28 cm disc on the bench, leaving a plump 1.5 cm border.
Spread a thin layer of the sauce, keeping it free from the border; scatter over the mozzarella.
Slide the pizza onto the steel; bake 5–7 minutes until bulbs of char appear on the rim and the base sets.
Finish off the oven with the remaining oil and the basil; repeat for the second pizza.

description: Roman pasta emulsified from egg yolks, Pecorino Romano, crisp guanciale and black pepper — famously with no cream.

ingredients.amount: to taste — plus more to finish
ingredients.name: black peppercorns, freshly crushed

ingredients.amount: to taste, use less than usual
ingredients.name: salt, for the pasta water

name: Pasta alla carbonara
steps: Start the pasta water — do keep salting low; guanciale and pecorino carry plenty of salt.
Cut the guanciale into strips | render in a cold, dry heavy pan over medium heat until glassy and golden with the fat clear, 8–10 minutes. Lift out with a slotted spoon, keep the fat in the pan.
In a bowl whisk the yolks with the Pecorino Romano and a storm of crushed black pepper until a thick paste forms.
Cook the spaghetti in the boiling water until just al dente; scoop out and reserve a full cup of the pasta water.
Off the heat, whisk a few tablespoons of hot pasta water into the yolk paste to loosen it — this “tempers” the yolks.
Tip the drained pasta into the pan with the guanciale fat, tossing to gloss; remove the pan from the burner entirely.
Add the loosened yolk mixture and toss hard, loosening with pasta water by the splash until the sauce is lacquered and sheet-like — never scrambled eggs.
Return the crisp guanciale, keeping a few crisp tops for garnish; serve immediately with extra Pecorino Romano and pepper.

description: Baked pasta sheets layered with slow meat ragù, silky béchamel and Parmigiano, a Sunday-table classic of Emilia-Romagna.

ingredients.name: whole milk, for the ragù finish

name: Lasagne al forno
steps: Make the ragù: sweat the pancetta in the olive oil 5 minutes, then add the onion, carrot and celery over medium heat 10–12 minutes until soft and translucent.
Brown the beef and pork a handful at a time until deeply caramelised, then deglaze with the white wine and reduce fully.
Add the garlic, the passata, a cup of water and salt; part-lid and simmer gently at least 2 hours, topping up with water if it thickens too fast.
Finish the ragù with the whole milk and the butter off the heat, stir, and rest.
Make the béchamel: melt the butter, blend in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the warm milk a ladleful at a time; season with salt and nutmeg, simmer 4–5 minutes until creamy.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C fan / 210 °C static. Butter a 30 × 22 cm baking dish.
Layer: thin béchamel, pasta sheets, ragù, béchamel, Parmigiano — repeat 4 times, finishing with the remaining béchamel and a thick veil of Parmigiano.
Bake 40–45 minutes until deep golden on top and bubbling at the edges; rest 15 minutes at room temperature before cutting.

description: Saffron-golden stirred rice finished with butter and Parmesan, the credential dish of Milanese cooking.

ingredients.amount: a good pinch, about 15–20 threads, soaked in a small cup of the hot stock
ingredients.name: saffron threads

ingredients.amount: to taste, mind the saltiness of your stock
ingredients.name: salt

name: Risotto alla milanese
steps: Bring the stock to a bare simmer in a pot; put the saffron into a cup of the hot stock to steep.
In a wide pan melt 70 g of the butter (plus marrow, if using); add onion with a pinch of salt, cook 6–8 minutes until translucent without colouring.
Stir in the rice and toast 2–3 minutes until edges look glassy.
Add wine and let it evaporate fully.
Add a ladle of hot stock, stirring constantly as it absorbs; keep adding by the ladle, stirring, for 14–16 minutes.
Add the saffron stock and continue ladling until the rice is al dente and the texture ripples like a wave — all’onda.
Off heat, beat in the remaining 40 g cold butter and the Parmigiano; correct salt, rest covered 2 minutes.
Serve on flat warmed plates

description: Layers of fried aubergine, tomato sauce, mozzarella and basil baked until melting — Southern Italian comfort cooking par excellence.

ingredients.name: sunflower or olive oil, for shallow frying
extra-virgin olive oil, for the sauce
fior di latte or mozzarella, torn and well drained

name: Parmigiana di melanzane
steps: Slice aubergines lengthwise about 1 cm thick, salt generously on both sides and drain on a rack 30–40 minutes; pat completely dry.
Make the sauce: warm the olive oil with the garlic and a pinch of peperoncino (optional), add the passata and salt; simmer 20 minutes with a few basil leaves.
Dredge the aubergine slices in flour, shaking off excess, and fry about 2 minutes per side in wide shallow oil until golden; drain on a rack.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
In a ceramic dish, layer sauce, aubergine, mozzarella, Parmigiano and basil; repeat 3–4 layers, finishing with sauce and Parmigiano.
Bake 35–40 minutes until bubbling and golden; rest 15–20 minutes before serving warm or at room temperature.

description: Beef braised for hours in Burgundy red wine with lardons, pearl onions and mushrooms — Burgundian slow cooking at its classic best.
name: Boeuf bourguignon
steps: Brown the bacon, then sear the beef in batches and set aside.
Soften the onions and carrots in the same pot, stir in the flour and tomato paste, then pour in the wine and add the herbs.
Return the meat, cover and braise in a 160 °C oven for 2½–3 hours.
Sauté the mushrooms in butter and stir them in for the last 20 minutes.

description: Provençal stewed medley of aubergine, courgette, peppers, tomato, herbs and generous olive oil.

ingredients.name: red and green peppers, in 2 cm strips
ripe tomatoes, chopped (or tinned plum tomatoes)

name: Ratatouille
steps: Warm 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a wide, heavy pot; cook the onion with a pinch of salt over medium heat 8 minutes until soft, then add garlic and peppers 8 minutes more.
Add aubergine with remaining oil; let it collapse and pick up some colour, 10 minutes, stirring only occasionally.
Stir in the courgette, cook 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, thyme, bay; season, part-cover and simmer gently 20–25 minutes until thick and glossy, stirring occasionally.
Remove the herbs; adjust salt, pepper and a final thread of olive oil.
Serve warm, at room temperature or chilled — flavour best matures the next day.

description: Chicken braised with wine, bacon lardons, aromatic vegetables and herbs — the classic marinated French stew.
name: Coq au vin
steps: Brown the bacon, then the seasoned chicken pieces; set aside.
Fry the onions, mushrooms and garlic, stir in the flour and add the wine and herbs.
Return the chicken and simmer gently for about 45 minutes until tender.
Reduce the sauce slightly and serve hot.

description: Open tart of rich shortcrust, savoury egg custard and lardons from Lorraine — the original contains no cheese.
name: Quiche Lorraine
steps: Blind-bake the pastry case for 12 minutes at 190 °C.
Fry the lardons until golden and scatter them in the case with the cheese.
Whisk the eggs, cream, milk and nutmeg, pour over and bake 30–35 minutes until just set.

description: Paper-thin pancakes folded around sweet or savoury fillings, Brittany’s famous crêpe cooked on a fast-hot billig plate.
name: Crêpes
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, butter, sugar and salt into a smooth thin batter and rest 15 minutes.
Heat a lightly buttered pan and pour in a thin layer of batter, tilting to coat.
Cook about 1 minute per side and fill with sugar, lemon or jam.

description: Valencian saffron socarrat rice cooked in its wide shallow pan with chicken, rabbit, green beans and butter beans.
name: Paella
steps: Brown the chicken in olive oil in a wide pan, then add the pepper, garlic and tomatoes and cook down.
Stir in the paprika and rice, then pour in the hot stock with the saffron.
Simmer without stirring for 15 minutes, nestle in the seafood and cook 5 more minutes.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

description: Thick potato-and-onion omelette fried in olive oil in the base egg dish of Spanish home kitchens.

ingredients.name: waxy potatoes, peeled and in 3 mm slices
olive oil, for poaching the potatoes

name: Tortilla española
steps: Pat the potatoes dry, then drop into plenty of olive oil over medium-low heat — it should bubble lazily, not fry hard.
Poach the potatoes with the onion and ½ tsp salt 18–20 minutes until fork-tender and pale gold; drain well, reserving the oil.
Beat the eggs with ½ tsp salt in a big bowl; fold in the drained potatoes and let them soak 5 minutes.
Wipe the pan, add 2 tbsp of the reserved oil; pour in the mix and cook over medium-low 3–4 minutes until the edges set.
Plate-and-flip: invert the semi-set tortilla onto a plate, slide it back pale side down; cook 3 minutes more.
Slide onto a plate, let rest 5 minutes, and serve in wedges — warm or at room temperature.

description: Chilled Andalusian raw-tomato soup blitzed with pepper, cucumber, bread, garlic, olive oil and sherry vinegar.
name: Gazpacho andaluz
steps: Chop the vegetables and soak the bread briefly in water.
Blend everything with the oil and vinegar until very smooth, then season.
Chill at least 2 hours and serve cold with a drizzle of olive oil.

description: Fried potato cubes dressed with fiery bravas sauce, the classic tapa of Barcelona and Madrid bars.
name: Patatas bravas
steps: Cut the potatoes into chunks and roast or fry in olive oil until golden and crisp.
Simmer the garlic, paprikas, tomato paste, vinegar and a little water into a thick spicy sauce.
Spoon the sauce over the hot potatoes and serve.

description: Ridged fried pastry ropes dusted in sugar and dunked in thick drinking chocolate.
name: Churros con chocolate
steps: Boil the water with sugar and salt, add the flour and beat to a smooth dough; cool slightly and beat in the egg.
Pipe strips into hot oil and fry until golden, then drain and roll in sugar.
Melt the chocolate with the milk for dipping.

description: Vinegared rice matched to raw fish, wrapped or pressed — the maki-roll technique is the classic home-style branch of sushi.
name: Sushi
steps: Rinse and cook the rice, then season it with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt and cool.
Spread rice on nori, add strips of fish and cucumber, then roll tightly with a mat.
Slice with a wet knife and serve with soy sauce and wasabi.

description: Wheat noodles in deep meat-and-shiitake-Soysauce-style broth topped with chashu pork, egg and aromatics.
name: Ramen
steps: Simmer the broth with the soy sauce and miso.
Soft-boil the eggs for 6½ minutes, peel and halve them; sear the pork slices.
Cook the noodles, divide into bowls, ladle over the broth and top with pork, egg, spring onion and nori.

description: Seafood and vegetables in a whisper-thin ice-cold batter fried quickly at high heat.
name: Tempura
steps: Pat the prawns and sliced vegetables dry.
Lightly mix the flour, egg and ice-cold water — leave it lumpy.
Dip and fry in 180 °C oil in small batches until pale golden, then drain and serve at once with dipping sauce.

description: “As-you-like-it” cabbage pancake in the Osaka style — batter, sauce, mayonnaise and dancing bonito flakes.

ingredients.name: thinly sliced pork belly (or bacon), 2 slices per pancake

name: Okonomiyaki
steps: Dissolve the dashi powder in hot water; cool at least 10 minutes while you shred the cabbage fine.
Whisk flour with the cooled dashi and the eggs to a soft batter; fold in the cabbage, beni shōga and half the aonori.
Heat a wide pan greased with 2 tbsp oil over medium; pour half the batter, mound it 2 cm thick and press into a circle about 18 cm wide.
Lay 2 slices of pork belly over each pancake; cook 4–5 minutes until the base is browned.
Flip gently (pork side down), cover and cook 5–6 minutes; flip once more and crisp 2 minutes.
Slide onto plates; brush with okonomiyaki sauce, zigzag mayonnaise, scatter aonori and a dramatic pile of katsuobushi.

description: Light dashi broth dissolved with fermented soybean miso paste and everyday seasonal add-ins.
name: Miso soup
steps: Heat the water with the dashi.
Add the tofu and wakame and warm through.
Take off the heat, dissolve the miso in a ladleful of broth and stir in; finish with spring onion. Do not boil.

description: Imperial roast duck with lacquered skin served with thin pancakes, scallion, cucumber and sweet bean sauce.
name: Peking duck
steps: Scald the duck with boiling water, dry it and brush with the honey, soy and vinegar; air-dry in the fridge overnight if possible.
Roast at 180 °C for about 1 hour 45 minutes until the skin is deep brown and crisp.
Slice the skin and meat and serve with pancakes, cucumber, spring onion and hoisin.

description: Hand-wrapped dumplings with juicy pork-and-chive filling, boiled and eaten traditionally for Lunar New Year.
name: Jiaozi
steps: Knead the flour and water into a smooth dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the pork, finely chopped salted cabbage, soy sauce, sesame oil and ginger.
Roll small rounds, fill, fold and pleat, then boil 6–7 minutes or pan-fry then steam.

description: Sichuan classic of silky tofu and minced pork, fiery with doubanjiang and numbing with Sichuan pepper.

ingredients.name: silken or soft tofu, in 2.5 cm cubes
cornstarch slurry (1 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp water)
spring onions, sliced thin, greens separated

name: Mapo tofu
steps: Blanch the tofu cubes in lightly salted simmering water 2 minutes and hold in warm water (they firming and lose the beany bite).
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high; fry the minced pork, breaking it up, until crumbly and browned, 4–5 minutes.
Scoot the meat aside, add doubanjiang, douchi (if used), garlic, ginger and the white part of spring onions; fry until the oil glows brick-red.
Add the Shaoxing around the pan rim; pour in stock and soy sauce and bring to a simmer.
Drain the tofu and slide it in; simmer gently 4–5 minutes, nudging rather than stirring.
Stir the slurry and add half; after 30 seconds add the rest and fold until the sauce thickly clings to the tofu.
Scatter with spring-onion greens and Sichuan pepper; taste (salt, more málà to taste) and serve with rice.

description: Wok-fired cubed chicken with crisp peanuts chillies and Sichuan peppercorn in Guizhou-style sweet-sour balance.
name: Kung Pao chicken
steps: Marinate the chicken with half the soy sauce and the cornflour.
Stir-fry the chillies, garlic and ginger briefly, then add the chicken and cook through.
Add the remaining soy, vinegar and sugar, toss with the peanuts and serve with rice.

description: Day-old rice tossed over high heat with eggs, crisp vegetables and light seasoning — Yangzhou is the canonical template.
name: Fried rice
steps: Scramble the eggs in hot oil and set aside.
Stir-fry the vegetables, then add the cold rice and fry until it starts to crisp.
Return the eggs, add the soy sauce and spring onion and toss.

description: Layered slow steaming of saffron-scented par-boiled rice over marinated spiced meat finished dum-cooked under a sealed lid.
name: Biryani
steps: Marinate the meat in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste and spices for at least 1 hour.
Fry the onions until deep golden; par-boil the rice with whole spices.
Layer meat, rice, fried onions, herbs and saffron milk in a heavy pot, seal and cook on low heat for 35–40 minutes.

description: Delhi dish of tandoor-kissed chicken folded into a tomato-butter-cream sauce with kasuri methi.

ingredients.name: tomato purée (from about 500 g fresh or tinned tomatoes)
cashew nuts (optional — blend into sauce for thickness)

name: Butter chicken
steps: Mix chicken with yogurt, half the ginger-garlic paste, half the chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, turmeric, salt and lemon; marinate at least 1 hour (overnight in the fridge is ideal).
Broil, grill or pan-sear the chicken in a hot pan until charred in places and just cooked; set aside.
Melt half the butter over medium heat; fry the remaining ginger-garlic paste 1 minute, add tomato purée, remaining chilli powder and 1 tsp garam masala; simmer 10 minutes, stirring.
Blend the sauce smooth (with the cashews, if using) and return to the pan; simmer 5 minutes to thicken.
Stir in the cream, sugar and the rest of the butter; add the chicken and any resting juices and simmer gently 5 minutes.
Crush kasuri methi between your palms over the pan, stir, adjust salt, and rest off-heat 2 minutes before serving with naan or rice.

description: Crisp fermented rice-and-lentil crepe wrapped around potato masala, served with coconut chutney and sambar.
name: Masala dosa
steps: Soak the rice and dal, grind to a batter and ferment overnight.
Make the filling: pop mustard seeds, fry onion and chilli, add turmeric and mashed boiled potato.
Spread the batter thin on a hot griddle, cook until crisp, fill and fold.

description: Fresh spinach purée made saag-style, wok-spiced and loaded with soft cubes of paneer griddled-cheese.
name: Palak paneer
steps: Blanch the spinach and blend to a purée.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger, add chopped tomatoes and spices, and cook down.
Stir in the spinach and cream, add the paneer and simmer 5 minutes.

description: Triangular pastry fried with spiced potato-pea fillings, an essential South-Asian street and teatime snack.
name: Samosa
steps: Make a firm dough from the flour, oil, salt and water; rest 30 minutes.
Cook the diced potatoes and peas with the cumin, chilli and garam masala for the filling.
Shape cones from the dough, fill, seal and deep-fry on medium heat until golden.

description: Steamed semolina granules crowned with stewed vegetables, meat and spiced broth — Friday’s family tradition in the Maghreb.
name: Moroccan couscous
steps: Brown the meat with the onions and spices, add the water and carrots and simmer for 40 minutes.
Add the courgettes and chickpeas for the last 15 minutes.
Steam the couscous with a little oil and butter and serve topped with the stew.

description: Slow-simmered chicken with preserved lemon, green olives, ginger and saffron in the conical clay pot.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs, bone-in, skin-on (or halved breast)

ingredients.amount: a pinch, bloomed in 2 tbsp warm water
ingredients.name: saffron threads

name: Chicken tagine
steps: Rub the chicken with oil, garlic, ginger, turmeric, paprika and salt; marinate 30 minutes while you slice the onion.
Spread the onion slices over the base of the tagine or casserole; lay the chicken on top with the herb stems, cinnamon-free.
Add the saffron water and loosen with about 250 ml water; cover with the lid.
Simmer gently over low heat 40 minutes, undisturbed, until the chicken is tender and the onion has melted into a sauce.
Add the olives and preserved lemon; uncover and simmer 10–15 minutes to concentrate the sauce.
Finish with chopped coriander, parsley and black pepper; ladle from the centre of the pot with warm bread.

description: Fez pastry of crisp warqa leaves filled with pigeon or chicken, almonds, cinnamon and a sugar veil.
name: Pastilla
steps: Simmer the chicken with the onion and spices until tender, shred it and reduce the sauce, stirring in the eggs to set.
Fry the almonds and mix with sugar and cinnamon.
Layer buttered pastry with the chicken and almond fillings, fold into a parcel and bake at 200 °C until golden; dust with sugar and cinnamon.

description: Tomato-lentil-chickpea soup enlivened with herbs and thin vermicelli, the fasting-day soup of Ramadan in Morocco.
name: Harira
steps: Fry the meat and onion with the spices, add celery, tomatoes and lentils and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and vermicelli.
Whisk the flour with water, stir in to thicken and finish with fresh herbs and lemon.

description: Shredded msemen pastry soaked in spiced ras-el-hanout chicken lentil and fenugreek broth, served for family celebrations.
name: Rfissa
steps: Simmer the chicken with the onions, lentils and spices until tender.
Shred the flatbread into small pieces and arrange on a large dish.
Pour over the broth, top with the chicken and lentils.

description: Cairo street carb of rice, brown lentils, macaroni and chickpeas under tomato sauce, garlic-vinegar and crispyfried onions.

ingredients.name: chickpeas, cooked or canned and drained
vegetable oil, for deep-frying the onions

name: Koshari
steps: Simmer the lentils in salted water 25 minutes until just tender; drain and keep warm. Cook the rice in plenty of boiling water 12 minutes; drain, rest covered and keep warm.
Boil the macaroni until al dente; drain and rinse briefly under warm water.
Warm the chickpeas in the same pan, drain them; toss them into ¼ of the cumin mixture.
Make the tomato sauce: fry half the garlic until golden, add passata, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp cumin and salt; bubble 8 minutes.
Make the da’ah: gently fry remaining garlic seconds, then blend with 2 tbsp vinegar, half-teaspoon cumin, and crushed chilli in a small pot heated 1 minute.
Toss the onion rounds with flour and fry in hot oil until deep golden and brittle; drain on paper.
Assemble a mound of rice, lentils and macaroni; scatter chickpeas; ladle on the hot tomato sauce, dash the da’ah, and crown with spoonfuls of crisp onion.

description: Egypt’s breakfast staple: slow-simmered fava beans mashed with olive oil, lemon, garlic and cumin.
name: Ful medames
steps: Warm the beans gently with a splash of their liquid and mash lightly.
Stir in crushed garlic, lemon juice, cumin and half the olive oil.
Serve topped with chopped tomato, parsley and the remaining oil with warm bread.

description: Velvety jute-leaf stew, garlic-chilli-tempered, spooned over rice or chicken — the defining taste of an Egyptian household.
name: Molokhia
steps: Simmer the chicken in the stock until cooked; keep the broth.
Add the finely chopped molokhia to the hot broth and cook briefly — do not boil hard.
Fry the garlic with the coriander until golden and stir it in. Serve with rice.

description: Egyptian falafel made from herbed, spiced fava unbeans instead of chickpeas, fried green-in-the-middle.
name: Taameya
steps: Grind the drained beans with the herbs, onion, garlic and spices into a coarse paste.
Shape into small patties and coat with sesame seeds.
Deep-fry until deep golden and serve in pita with salad.

description: Feast plate of layered crisp bread, garlic-tomato sauce and slow-cooked lamb, the Eid celebration dish in big families.
name: Fatta
steps: Simmer the meat until tender; keep the broth.
Toast the pita pieces until crisp and cook the rice with the broth.
Layer pita, rice and meat, pour over a garlic-vinegar tomato sauce and top with yogurt.

description: West African one-pot long-grain rice steeped in smoky tomato-pepper base, the single most argued-over dish in the region.

ingredients.name: long-grain parboiled rice (e.g. golden perfume rice)

name: Jollof rice
steps: Blend tomatoes, bell pepper, Scotch bonnet, half the onion, garlic and ginger to a smooth sauce base.
Fry the sliced onion in the oil until golden; add tomato paste and fry 4–5 minutes until it darkens and the oil turns red around it.
Add the blended base, curry powder, thyme, bay and bouillon; simmer 15 minutes until thick and glossy, stirring now and then.
Stir the washed rice through the base; add 600 ml hot water and salt, and bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce to low, cover, and steam 18 minutes; do not lift the lid.
Lay foil over the pot, clamp on the lid, and steam 8–10 minutes more; then fork through and rest 5 minutes before serving.

description: Thick melon-seed stew thickened with leafy spinach, assorted meats and dried fish — scooped up by hand with swallow at every Nigerian gathering.
name: Egusi soup
steps: Boil the meat with onion and seasoning until tender.
Fry the blended tomato, onion and pepper in palm oil, then stir in the egusi paste and cook into curds.
Add the meat, fish and stock, simmer 20 minutes, then stir in the greens.

description: Stretchy swallow staple boiled and hand-beaten from yam tubers, used to scoop Nigerian stews by hand.
name: Pounded yam
steps: Peel and cut the yam and boil in water until very soft.
Pound or beat in a mortar or food processor until completely smooth, stretchy and lump-free.
Shape into balls and serve with egusi or another soup.

description: Thin beef skewers dusted in groundnut-based yaji spice and smoked over open coals, the nightly street snack of the north.
name: Suya
steps: Mix the ground peanuts with the spices to make the suya rub.
Coat the beef strips with oil and the rub, thread onto skewers and rest 30 minutes.
Grill on high heat for 8–10 minutes, turning, and serve with raw onion and tomato.

description: Deep-fried black-eyed-bean fritters lightened on groundnut-vegetable frying in peppered, airy batter.
name: Akara
steps: Blend the peeled peas with the onion and pepper and a little water into a thick fluffy paste.
Whisk the batter well to add air.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry until deep golden.

description: Grilled beef patty dressed in a soft bun — a German-American invention that became the national fast-cook of choice.

ingredients.name: lettuce leaves (or ½ onion in rings, raw or charred)

name: Hamburger
steps: Divide the mince into 2 equal portions and press gently into 2 cm-thick patties with a shallow dimple in the middle. Season the outsides just before cooking.
Split and butter the buns; toast them cut-side down in a hot pan until golden, and set aside.
Cook the patties in the same hot pan 3 minutes without moving, then flip and cook 2–3 minutes more to your preferred doneness (use a thermometer if unsure).
Top each patty with cheese (if used) and cover with a lid or plate 1 minute so the cheese melts.
Spread mayonnaise on both bun halves, stack tomato, patty, pickles and lettuce between them and press gently to seal.
Serve hot, with the juices pooling where they land.

description: Pork spare ribs marrow-toned for hours over hardwood smoke, enveloped in spicy-sweet sauce in many regional styles.
name: Barbecue ribs
steps: Remove the membrane from the ribs and rub with the sugar, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Wrap in foil and bake at 140 °C for about 2½–3 hours until tender.
Unwrap, brush with sauce and finish under the grill or on the barbecue for 10 minutes.

description: Baked elbow macaroni in rich cheddar sauce, a Colonial-era Thomas-Jefferson import turned comfort staple.
name: Mac and cheese
steps: Cook the macaroni until just tender and drain.
Make a roux of butter and flour, whisk in the milk to a smooth sauce, then melt in most of the cheese and mustard.
Combine with the pasta, top with cheese and breadcrumbs and bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes.

description: Creamy New-England chowder of clams, salt pork, potato and onion ladled deep along the Atlantic coast.
name: Clam chowder
steps: Fry the bacon, onion and celery, stir in the flour and add the potatoes and clam juice.
Simmer until the potatoes are tender, then add the milk and cream.
Add the clams, heat gently 5 minutes and season.

description: Double-crusted apple pie spiced with cinnamon and nutmeg — the dessert the country built its mythic status around.
name: Apple pie
steps: Line a pie dish with half the pastry.
Toss sliced apples with sugar, cinnamon and flour, pile in and dot with butter.
Cover with the remaining pastry, seal, brush with egg and bake at 200 °C for 45 minutes.

description: Chilli-achiote-marinated pork crowned with charred pineapple, fresh corn tortillas, onion and coriander — the Lebanese-migrant classic of Mexican bars.

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder, in thin slices
dried guajillo chillies, seeded and rehydrated in hot water
salsa de árbol or other hot salsa (optional)

name: Tacos (al pastor)
steps: Blend the drained chillies with achiote, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, cumin and salt until smooth; push through a sieve if grainy.
Coat the pork in the marinade, press into an even layer and refrigerate at least 4 hours (overnight is best).
Bring the meat close to freezing (30–40 minutes in the freezer) then slice as razor-thin as you can manage.
Sear the slices in batches over high heat, undisturbed, until crisp and caramelised at the edges, 2–3 minutes per side.
Grill the pineapple slices 2 minutes until char-marked, then dice small; char the tortillas 20 seconds per side over flame or comal.
Two tortillas per taco; fill with the pork, diced pineapple, onion and coriander; serve with lime and salsa.

description: Puebla’s celebratory sauce of dried chillies, nuts, spices and chocolate poured over turkey at civic feasts.
name: Mole poblano
steps: Toast and soak the chillies.
Fry the nuts, seeds, raisins, bread, onion and tomato and blend with the chillies and stock into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste, add the chocolate and spices and simmer for about 45 minutes.
Poach or roast the chicken and serve covered in the mole.

description: Hominy-and-pork stew red or green, simmered for hours and garnished tableside with lime, radish, lettuce and oregano.
name: Pozole
steps: Simmer the pork with half the onion and the garlic until tender, about 2 hours.
Soak and blend the chillies into a sauce and add with the hominy to the broth; simmer 30 minutes.
Serve with cabbage, radish, onion, oregano and lime.

description: Steamed corn dough parcels with meat or chilli fillings wrapped in husks, the ancient Mesoamerican portable meal.
name: Tamales
steps: Soak the husks in warm water.
Whip the fat, then beat in the masa, baking powder and stock into a soft dough.
Spread dough on a husk, add filling and salsa, fold and steam for about 1 hour.

description: Poblano chiles filled with fruit-and-meat picadillo, dressed in walnut sauce and pomegranate seeds in the flag colours.
name: Chiles en nogada
steps: Roast, peel and slit the chillies.
Cook the meat with the diced fruit and spices for the filling and stuff the chillies.
Coat in beaten egg and flour and fry; blend the walnuts, cream and cheese into a sauce.
Cover with the walnut sauce and scatter with pomegranate seeds.

description: Québécois plate: fresh-cut fries under squeaky cheese curds, drowned in brown gravy — a rural tavern origin turned national symbol.

ingredients.name: russet potatoes, cut into 1.5 cm fries, rinsed
fresh cheese curds, at room temperature
rich beef or chicken stock (or a 50/50 mix), warm

name: Poutine
steps: Heat the frying oil to 160 °C. Fry the potatoes in batches 6–7 minutes until pale and bendy; drain on a rack and rest 10 minutes.
Meanwhile make the gravy: melt the butter, whisk in the flour, and cook over medium heat 3–4 minutes to a sandy blond roux.
Whisk in the warm stock gradually; add Worcestershire and ketchup (if used) and simmer 8–10 minutes until spoon-coating; season.
Raise the oil temperature to 190 °C; fry the potatoes again 2–3 minutes to a deep gold that cracks, then drain and salt.
Pile the hot fries in warmed bowls; scatter the curds through them, then drown in lava-hot gravy and serve immediately.

description: Deep pork-and-potato meat pie spiced with cinnamon and clove, cheese heritage of Quebec and Acadian Christmas tables.
name: Tourtière
steps: Cook the meat with onion, potato, spices and stock until thick; cool.
Line a pie dish with pastry, add the filling and cover with a pastry lid.
Brush with egg and bake at 200 °C for about 40 minutes until golden.

description: Salt-brined, spice-cured smoked beef brisket hand-carved onto rye with yellow mustard, the szárazdeli icon of Montreal.
name: Montreal smoked meat sandwich
steps: Steam or warm the brisket until hot and tender.
Pile it generously onto mustard-spread rye bread.
Serve with a dill pickle on the side.

description: Canada’s sweet signature: flaky tart shell filled with sugar-butter-egg runny caramel — raisins or nuts optional and hotly debated.
name: Butter tarts
steps: Cut pastry rounds and press into a muffin tin.
Whisk the melted butter, sugar, syrup and egg and add the raisins.
Fill the cases two-thirds full and bake at 190 °C for 15–18 minutes.

description: Fried or baked flatbread adopted by Indigenous nations during the fur trade, cooked over fire, pan or oven.
name: Bannock
steps: Mix the dry ingredients and rub in the fat.
Stir in the water to form a soft dough and pat into a disc about 2 cm thick.
Pan-fry on low heat 8–10 minutes per side or bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes.

description: Brazil’s slow black bean and pork’s stew for Wednesday gatherings and Saturday family feasts, served with farofa and orange.
name: Feijoada
steps: Simmer the beans with the meats and bay leaves for 2 hours until everything is tender.
Fry the onion and garlic and stir a ladle of beans into them, mashing to thicken.
Serve with rice, collard greens and orange slices.

description: Fish stewed in coconut milk, palm oil, peppers and dendê oil in a clay pot — Bahia’s African-South American synthesis.
name: Moqueca
steps: Marinate the fish with lime, salt and garlic.
Layer sliced onion, pepper and tomato in a pot, add the fish and prawns and pour over the coconut milk and palm oil.
Simmer gently for 15–20 minutes and finish with coriander.

description: Chewy tapioca-flour pockets puffed with egg and Minas cheese — crisp outside, molten-within, eaten warm for breakfast.

ingredients.name: Minas cheese (or mozzarella/parmesan mix), finely grated

name: Pão de queijo
steps: Put the tapioca starch in a big bowl. Boil the milk with the oil and salt; pour it hot over the starch, stir, and rest 10 minutes until warm.
Beat in the eggs one by one, then the grated cheese; knead with patience until the dough is pliable, sticky but smooth.
Roll into 3 cm balls (about 20), placed on a lined tray 3 cm apart; rest in the fridge 15 minutes so they keep their shape.
Chill the tray briefly, then bake at 200 °C for 18–22 minutes until puffed and faintly golden — hollow-echo crisp when tapped — and serve hot.

description: Black-eyed pea fritters fried in dendê palm oil and stuffed with sautéed shrimp and vatapá — Bahian street-food royalty.
name: Acarajé
steps: Blend the peas with the onion and salt to a thick paste and beat until fluffy.
Shape into ovals and deep-fry in hot palm oil until golden.
Split open and fill with the shrimp and spicy paste.

description: The southern grasslands fire-ritual: skewered cuts of beef salted simply, carved at the table churrascaria-style.
name: Brazilian churrasco
steps: Cut the beef into thick steaks, season generously with coarse salt and thread onto skewers.
Grill over charcoal or high heat, turning, until browned outside and cooked to taste.
Slice thinly at the table and serve with farofa and vinaigrette.

description: Slow ember-grilled beef cuts cooked for hours at low distance, salted when warm and served with chimichurri and salad.
name: Asado
steps: Light the coals and let them burn down to even embers.
Season the meat with coarse salt and cook slowly on the grill, turning occasionally.
Rest and slice, then serve with chimichurri.

description: Half-moon pasties baked or fried with beef picadillo, egg, and olives — Tucumán or Salta folds give away the recipe geography.
name: Empanadas
steps: Make a dough with the flour, fat, salt and warm water; rest 30 minutes.
Cook the beef and onions with the spices; cool and fold in chopped egg and olives.
Cut rounds, fill, fold and crimp, brush with egg and bake at 200 °C until golden.

description: Thin breaded beef cutlets rendered golden in a pan and brightened with lemon, an Argentine table regular of Italian ancestry.
name: Milanesa
steps: Pound the cutlets thin and season with salt and garlic.
Dip in beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry until golden on both sides and serve with lemon.

description: Andean maize-and-white-bean stew with squash, beef and chorizo, traditionally cooked on May-25 patriotic toasts.
name: Locro
steps: Simmer the corn and beans with the beef for about 1½ hours.
Add the pumpkin and chorizo and cook until everything is soft and thick.
Top with a fried onion and paprika sauce.

description: Split grilled Argentine chorizo in a crusty roll, cascade the pan with salsa criolla or chimichurri at every pre-asado gathering.

ingredients.amount: a big pinch for the chimichurri
ingredients.name: salt

name: Choripán
steps: Make the chimichurri: fold parsley, garlic, oregano, chilli, vinegar and salt into the oil; rest at least 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Set the grill with a low flame and a medium zone; cook the chorizos 10–12 minutes, rolling for even char-splits.
Split each sausage by its end (butterfly coast) and toast it on the hot bars for a minute more.
Split the rolls, warm cut sides on the grill, and nestle in the sausage.
Open up with a flood of chimichurri — sauce running down the wrist is the correct way to eat it — and serve.

description: Fish flash-pickled in key lime with ají limo, red onion, cilantro, sweet potato and corn — Peru’s national treasure.

ingredients.name: firm white fish (corvina, sea bass, tilapia), skinless, in 2 cm cubes

ingredients.amount: about 200 ml fresh juice (6–8 limes), strained
ingredients.name: key limes or regular limes, juiced
ají limo chilli (or 1 small red chilli)
Giant Peruvian corn (choclo), boiled — or regular corn

ingredients.amount: seasoning the fish cubes first is essential
ingredients.name: salt

name: Ceviche
steps: Season the fish cubes with salt in a glass or ceramic bowl; let stand 2 minutes.
Soak the onion half-moons 10 minutes in cold water; drain well.
Pour on the lime juice to just submerge the fish; fold in chilli rings. Cure 2–3 minutes (traditional Lima style) until the fish turns milky-white at the edges.
Drain off most of the juice quickly (it can keep curing); fold in the onion and coriander.
Serve immediately as the tiger’s-milk (leche de tigre) still sizzles — with sweet potato and corn alongside.

description: Beef strips seared wok-hot with soy, onions and tomato, tossed with crisp fries and rice — the crisp high-born of Chifa cuisine.
name: Lomo saltado
steps: Marinate the beef strips with soy and vinegar.
Stir-fry in a very hot pan, then add the onions and tomatoes briefly.
Toss with the fries and serve with rice.

description: Shredded chicken in a creamy walnut-chilli (yellow aji amarillo) sauce thickened with bread and served over potatoes.
name: Ají de gallina
steps: Poach and shred the chicken.
Blend the soaked bread, milk, aji paste and walnuts into a creamy sauce and fry with the onion.
Stir in the chicken and serve over potatoes with egg.

description: Layered mashed golden potato with aji amarillo filled with tuna or shrimp salad; a true Limeño starter plate.
name: Causa limeña
steps: Boil and mash the potatoes with aji paste, lime juice, oil and salt into a smooth dough.
Mix the chicken or tuna with mayonnaise.
Layer potato, filling and avocado in a mould, chill and serve with egg.

description: Marinated skewers — traditionally beef heart — grilled Peru-style over coals, a colonial-era Inca-foods survivor.
name: Anticuchos
steps: Marinate the meat in aji panca, vinegar, garlic and cumin for at least 3 hours.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill over high heat for a few minutes per side, brushing with marinade, and serve with potato and corn.

description: The footy institution: hand-sized pie of rich minced beef gravy in crisp pastry, topped with tomato sauce.
name: Australian meat pie
steps: Brown the mince and onion, stir in the flour, stock and Worcestershire sauce and simmer until thick; cool.
Line individual tins with shortcrust, fill and top with puff pastry.
Brush with egg and bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes. Serve with tomato sauce.

description: Estuary fish cooked skin-crisp with a simple lemon dressing — the Australian catch best grilled when the freshest.
name: Barramundi
steps: Season the fillets and sear skin-side down in a hot pan for 4 minutes.
Flip, add butter and cook 2 minutes more, then squeeze over the lemon.
Serve with steamed green beans and parsley.

description: Swagman’s fire bread baked in coals: flour, butter, milk, salt kneaded and cooked on camp oven ash.
name: Damper
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and salt.
Stir in the liquid to a soft dough and shape into a round.
Slash the top and bake at 200 °C for 30–35 minutes until it sounds hollow when tapped.

description: Sponge squares dipped in chocolate and rolled in desiccated coconut, honouring Lady Lamington, Governor’s era of Christmas trees.
name: Lamington
steps: Cream butter, sugar and vanilla 3–4 minutes; beat in egg and vanilla until silky.
Fold in the self-raising flour alternately with the milk, ending on flour; spread the batter in an 18 cm square tin lined with baking paper.
Bake at 180 °C 25–30 minutes until brushed springy; cool in tin 10 minutes, then completely — ideally overnight, chilled.
Trim, then cut into 16 even squares.
Sift the icing sugar with the cocoa into a deep bowl; whisk in milk and boiling water to a smooth glaze.
Dip each square into the chocolate glaze with two forks, turning to coat fully, then roll in the coconut and set on a rack.
Rest on the rack 20 minutes so the coat sets before stacking or serving.

description: Crisp crumbed chicken breast under tomato sauce and molten cheese — the pub-night staple of Australian dining rooms.
name: Chicken parmigiana
steps: Dip the chicken in egg and breadcrumbs and fry until golden.
Place in a dish, cover with tomato sauce and cheeses.
Bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes until the cheese bubbles.

description: Māori earth-oven feast: meat and root vegetables steamed underground on heated stones wrapped in leaves for hours.
name: Hāngī
steps: Season the meat and place in foil-lined baskets; add the vegetables.
Cook in a pit oven with hot stones, or wrap tightly and cook in a covered oven at 180 °C.
Cook 3–4 hours until smoky and tender.

description: Bakery-counter classic: puck pastry lid of beef-and-gravy pie, grabbed from the dairy counter for generations.
name: New Zealand meat pie
steps: Cook the mince and onion with the flour and stock into a thick filling; cool.
Line the tins with shortcrust, add the filling and cover with puff pastry.
Brush with egg and bake at 200 °C for 25–30 minutes.

description: Fish batter-anointed fried straight, wrapped in newspaper alongside chips — the Friday-newspaper tradition shared by the entire South Pacific.
name: Fish and chips
steps: Cut the potatoes into thick chips and fry until pale, then fry again until crisp.
Whisk the flour and cold liquid into a batter, coat the fish and fry at 180 °C for 5–6 minutes.
Serve with lemon, salt and vinegar.

description: Meringue-shell shell crowned with whipped cream and fruit — named for ballerina Anna Pavlova, claimed with pride by both ANZAC nations.

ingredients.amount: about 350 g in mixed fruit to cover
ingredients.name: strawberries, kiwifruit, banana or passionfruit

name: Pavlova
steps: Preheat the oven to 120 °C; line a tray with baking paper and draw a 20 cm circle.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks; add sugar in spoonfuls, beating until glossy and the sugar fully dissolved (rub a pinch — no grains).
Fold in the cornflour and vinegar gently; spoon into the circle and carve a soft crater with a spoon.
Bake 60–75 minutes until the shell is firm to the tap; turn the oven off and let the pavlova cool inside with the door closed, about 1 hour.
Whip the chilled cream with vanilla to soft peaks; pile it into the crater.
Crown with the fruit and serve promptly — the shell softens once dressed.

description: Vanilla ice cream tumbled with crisp honey-toffee nuggets — at the movie cinema counter of dozens of neighbouring shops a NZ classic.
name: Hokey pokey ice cream
steps: Heat the milk and cream, whisk the yolks and sugar and combine into a custard; chill.
Churn in an ice-cream machine or freeze, stirring every hour.
Fold in the crushed honeycomb at the end.

description: Fijian raw fish “cooked” in lime and folded through coconut cream with onion and chilli — served cool in half-coconut shells.

ingredients.name: sushi-grade white fish, in 2 cm cubes
bird’s eye chillies (or 1 small red chilli), sliced

name: Kokoda
steps: Season the fish cubes and pour over the lime juice; cure covered in the fridge 1½–2 hours, stirring occasionally, until opaque.
Marinate the? — Drain the fish briefly, keeping only a spoonful of the juice.
Fold in the coconut milk, onion, chilli, cucumber and tomato; season and rest in the fridge 15 minutes.
Taste and adjust: a squeeze more lime, a pinch of salt, more chilli if you dare.
Finish with chopped herbs; serve chilled, scooped into half coconut shells if you have them.

description: Fijian oven-feast: wrapped chicken, pork, taro and breadfruit steaming under the earth for banquet day.
name: Lovo
steps: Wrap seasoned fish or meat and root vegetables in banana leaves or foil.
Cook in an earth oven over hot stones, or in a sealed oven at 180 °C.
Cook for about 2–3 hours and serve with coconut cream.

description: Taro leaves wrapped around coconut cream and steamed in banana leaves until meltingly soft across the South Pacific.
name: Palusami
steps: Mix the coconut cream with onion and salt.
Wrap spoonfuls in taro leaves or spinach, forming tight parcels.
Wrap in foil and bake at 180 °C for about 45 minutes.

description: Simmered taro leaves in thin coconut milk, classic village condiment served beside rice and fish.
name: Rourou
steps: Wash the leaves and simmer with the sliced onion until soft.
Add the coconut milk and cook gently for 15–20 minutes.
Season with salt and a squeeze of lime.

description: Grated cassava and coconut milk baked into a sticky-sweet slice, the warm community cake of Fijian afternoons.
name: Cassava cake
steps: Mix the grated cassava with the coconut milk, condensed milk, eggs, melted butter and sugar.
Pour into a greased pan and bake at 180 °C for about 1 hour.
Cool before slicing.
